dataQuality.scope: Verified public official-source intelligence snapshot integrating WOAH/FAO material with structured Directorate of Veterinary Services Weekly Highlights observations.
dataQuality.limitations: This is not a complete national outbreak line list. Weekly Highlight files were not available in the connected mailbox for every labelled week, and repeated weekly observations may describe continuing outbreaks rather than new outbreaks.
principles: unknown is not treated as zero
surveillance updates are not labelled as outbreaks unless the source confirms an outbreak
weekly repeated mentions are treated as time-series observations rather than automatically counted as separate outbreaks
country-level programme information is kept separate from event-level disease reports
source inconsistencies are retained with data-quality notes rather than silently corrected
property-level private identifiers from distributed Weekly Highlights are omitted from the public feed

events.summary: WOAH endorsed Zimbabwe's official control programme for dog-mediated rabies in 2026. The endorsement recognises the national control programme; it does not mean Zimbabwe is free from rabies.
events.notes: WOAH listed Zimbabwe among Members with an endorsed official control programme for dog-mediated rabies according to Resolution No. 27 of the 93rd General Session in May 2026.

events.summary: WOAH's evaluation of Zimbabwe's dog-mediated rabies control programme reported multi-year surveillance data, including 1,625 animal samples tested between 2018 and 2024, with a declining trend in the percentage of positive samples. Zimbabwe reported case definitions for human and animal rabies and use of IDSR/DHIS2 for related human surveillance and dog-bite reporting.
events.sourceTitle: Ad hoc Group evaluation of official control programmes for dog-mediated rabies
events.notes: The source discusses historical surveillance and programme performance. It is not a 2026 outbreak count.

events.summary: FAO's Sub-Saharan Africa HPAI situation update reported a multisectoral HPAI situational analysis in Zimbabwe and routine government surveillance in large commercial poultry farms, with samples submitted quarterly. The update also noted gaps in surveillance capacity and practices.
events.sourceOrganisation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
events.notes: The cited FAO update does not state that Zimbabwe had a confirmed HPAI outbreak in this item; therefore the feed records this as surveillance intelligence, not a confirmed outbreak.

events.summary: WOAH reported that new foot-and-mouth disease SAT 1 notifications were submitted by Zimbabwe during 2026 as part of a wider southern African spread of the serotype. WOAH's regional situation map was current to 26 August 2026. The cited article does not provide Zimbabwe-specific outbreak counts or localities, so those fields remain unknown rather than being inferred.
events.sourceTitle: The spread of FMD to new areas is concerning, but consequences could be worse
events.notes: WOAH stated that since early 2026 new FMD notifications were submitted by Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The source supports current reported FMD SAT 1 activity in Zimbabwe but does not provide a Zimbabwe-specific line list, counts or locality breakdown.

weeklyHighlights.note: Weekly data are partitioned by month for efficient incremental synchronization. Repeated weekly mentions are trend observations, not automatically new outbreaks.

diseaseProfiles.name: Rabies
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Dogs are the principal source of human dog-mediated rabies transmission
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Zimbabwe has a WOAH-endorsed official control programme for dog-mediated rabies and active national vaccination/surveillance.

diseaseProfiles.name: Anthrax
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Bacillus anthracis spores in contaminated environments and infected herbivores
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Endemic hotspot surveillance and vaccination are active; confirmed and suspected zoonotic events occurred in 2026.

diseaseProfiles.name: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Avian influenza viruses circulating in domestic and wild bird populations
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Zimbabwe conducts HPAI surveillance, including commercial poultry surveillance.

diseaseProfiles.name: Foot-and-mouth disease
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: FMD virus in susceptible cloven-hoofed domestic animals and wildlife; African buffalo are an important reservoir at the wildlife-livestock interface
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Sporadic 2026 outbreaks and laboratory detections were reported alongside vaccination, quarantine and movement-control measures.

diseaseProfiles.name: Lumpy skin disease
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Lumpy skin disease virus, with vector-associated transmission
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: A substantial seasonal 2026 wave declined as winter progressed.

diseaseProfiles.name: Tick-borne diseases
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Ticks transmitting Theileria, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and Babesia infections
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Major cattle morbidity and mortality were reported early in 2026, with declining activity after intensified dipping and seasonal cooling.

diseaseProfiles.name: Newcastle disease
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Outbreaks or suspected clusters occurred in Kariba, Nyanga and Murewa alongside national vaccination.

diseaseProfiles.name: Brucellosis
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Brucella infection in livestock with occupational and foodborne human exposure risk
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: National surveillance detected positive cattle in several districts during July 2026.

diseaseProfiles.name: Animal African Trypanosomiasis
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Trypanosoma spp. transmitted by tsetse flies
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Sentinel and communal herd surveillance detected T. brucei and T. vivax infections during 2026.

diseaseProfiles.name: Human African Trypanosomiasis
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense transmitted by tsetse flies
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Two r-HAT cases with one fatality were reported cumulatively in 2026 by the May/June surveillance reports.

diseaseProfiles.name: Peste des petits ruminants
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: PPR virus in sheep and goats
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Large-scale surveillance supports Zimbabwe's historical freedom dossier.

diseaseProfiles.name: Contagious bovine pleuropneumonia
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. mycoides in cattle
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Targeted surveillance supports preparation of an official disease-freedom dossier.

diseaseProfiles.name: Bovine cysticercosis (beef measles)
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Recurring detections were recorded through abattoir meat inspection.

diseaseProfiles.name: Hydatidosis (cystic echinococcosis)
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato cycle involving dogs and livestock
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Recurring offal condemnations were recorded through meat inspection.

diseaseProfiles.name: Avian influenza surveillance
diseaseProfiles.primaryReservoirOrSource: Influenza A viruses in avian hosts
diseaseProfiles.nationalContext: Laboratory submissions were recorded in 2026 without treating surveillance submissions as confirmed outbreaks.

provenance.warning: Always retain the distinction between confirmed outbreaks, suspected events, surveillance updates, programme status and contextual One Health information.
